idiom_name: one struct + renderJSON/renderHTML/renderCSV functions switched on Accept
implementation_notes: Go has no view objects to register: each representation is a plain function over the same struct - tmpl.Execute for html/template, json.NewEncoder(w).Encode, xml.NewEncoder(w).Encode, encoding/csv - and a short switch on the Accept header or on a format suffix chooses between them. html/template's contextual auto-escaping is what replaces the classic view helper, and json struct tags on a DTO are what replace the presentation model. Reach for an explicit registry/listener structure only for streaming fan-out (one broadcaster feeding several subscriber renderers), never for request/response handlers, which must not retain per-connection renderers.
pitfalls: Headers are frozen after the first write: set Content-Type before the first encode, and render into a bytes.Buffer when a renderer error must still be turned into an error response.
html/template only escapes values inside templates; embedding model data into an inline <script> with fmt.Fprintf reintroduces XSS - marshal it to JSON instead.

The same struct is not automatically the same model per format: json.Marshal skips unexported fields and html/template can call methods, so define one explicit DTO to keep the representations in step.
